emphasis_markers_in_non_math: This lesson follows [MIT OpenCourseWare, 18.01 Single Variable Calculus, Fall 2006, Lecture 19: First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-01-single-variable-calculus-fall-2006/817a2c46ddc23e2efda247a79ddeed34_lec19.pdf). The PDF has a cover and four numbered lecture pages. Printed page 1 supplies FTC1 and the power and positive-sine examples; page 2 supplies the rate interpretation and full sine cycle; page 3 supplies interval addition and reversed limits; page 4 supplies comparison, bounds on  and substitution. The explanations of conditions, the derivative argument for the linear exponential bound, the additional worked motion and decreasing-substitution cases, and Q1–Q6 are teaching additions. Figures are newly drawn to express the source's signed-area and interval relationships. This document teaches the antiderivative-evaluation result and its uses; it does not claim a formal proof of FTC.
